paper.title_en: Deterministic preparation of squeezed Schrödinger cat states with arbitrary size and squeezing
paper.abstract_en: We introduce a scheme for the deterministic preparation of squeezed Schrödinger cat states based on reservoir engineering. Our proposal relies on the linear and quadratic coupling of an oscillator mode to an auxiliary mode that decays into a vacuum reservoir. For suitable couplings, we show that the system unconditionally relaxes into a pure steady state. We derive an analytical expression for the steady state in terms of the coupling constants, and show that it corresponds to a displaced and squeezed finite superposition of Fock states. Numerical simulations further confirms that this state is reached with unit fidelity from a thermal initial state, without measurement, feedback or post-selection. Additionally, we derive analytical expressions for the non-Gaussianity and the Wigner function of the steady state. Our results reveal that states exhibiting maximal non-Gaussianity are excellent approximations of squeezed Schrödinger cat states, with fidelities exceeding $0.996$. The optimal squeezing stays close to 3dB, while the squared cat size scales proportionally with the highest Fock state occupation number in the finite superposition of the steady state. These maximally non-Gaussian states also maximise the Wigner logarithmic negativity. Finally, by selecting the appropriate ratios of the couplings, our scheme can generate cat states subject to arbitrary squeezing and displacement.
